# pcsc-tools

**Smartcard reader diagnostics — is the reader even working?**

- **Version recorded:** 1.7.3
- **Categories:** `rfid`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/LudovicRousseau/pcsc-tools>

## What it does

Utilities for PC/SC smartcard readers: listing readers, monitoring card insertion and removal, and identifying a card from its ATR against a public database.

## Why you would want it

It answers the first question in every contactless problem -- does the host see the reader at all -- separately from whether any card tooling works. pcsc_scan identifying a card by ATR is often the fastest route to knowing what you are holding.

## Before it will work

The pcscd daemon running, which the package pulls in, and a PC/SC- compatible reader.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`rfid`](../profiles/rfid.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install pcsc-tools --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `pcsc-tools`

## Known problems

pcscd and libnfc will fight over the same reader: whichever claims it first wins and the other reports no device. Stopping pcscd is the usual fix when libnfc tools suddenly stop seeing hardware, and it is the single most common confusion in this profile.
